# DEPS-GRADLE-CATALOG-1B — admission 3, revision 3 (answers review-2: F2-READ and F3-QUOTED-WRITE)

Both findings are fixed, and all four builder checks pass on the final tree. I ran each one verbatim, in the foreground, in this cycle. DGC-B04 printed `DGC-B04-OK`, and the field rows are the same as in the earlier cycles. No stop condition was hit, and nothing is committed.

Evidence is in `.agent-manager/slices/DEPS-GRADLE-CATALOG-1B/admission-3/iter3/`. The candidate is saved as `admission-3/candidate-iter3.patch`.

## The defects and the one rule that closes the class

The class is how the reader classifies each use of the map name. F1, F2 and F2-READ/F3 were all errors at one edge of that classification.

- **F2-READ:** `println libs` was counted, although it only renders the map as text.
- **F3:** `ext."libs" = …` was not seen as naming the map. An earlier admitted map then stayed readable with its old group, so the old group was reported as declared.

**The rule** (`gradle_catalog.rs`, `evaluate_alias_map`). Every use of the map name is exactly one of three things:

1. **An admitted literal statement.** It is evaluated in order.
2. **Proven not to write the map.** It is ignored. There are four kinds:
   - a key label `libs:` in another map or call;
   - one entry read that ends the expression, behind any receiver. This now includes `ext."libs".zstd`.
   - the map rendered as text (new: `rendered_as_text`). This is the whole of a `"${libs}"` interpolation, a `"$libs"` reference, or the sole argument of the script's own unqualified `print` / `println`.
   - a string literal `"libs"` that does not name the map as a property key.
3. **Anything else** — a write, or a use whose effect the reader cannot determine — makes the whole map unreadable.

A quoted property name after a navigation (`ext."libs"`, `ext.'libs'`, `ext?."libs"`, `ext.@'libs'`) now names the map as a property key, the same way a subscript key does (`string_names_map_key`).

**The reason shown.** I kept the record's wording, `alias map in {script}:{line} is not a top-level literal assignment`. The doc comments and the CLI contract no longer say that every counted use assigns. They now say that the note names the first statement that uses the map, is not an admitted literal assignment, and is not proven not to write it. They also say explicitly that the note does not claim the statement assigns.
